text:
harper: Hi all 44b. First day here. I'm on a Pixelbook running ChromeOS (Crostini / Debian Bullseye). Trying to follow the repo bootstrap but hitting a few weird Crostini-specific issues: no systemd so docker-compose can't talk to a daemon, asdf python/node builds fail with "pkg-config"/"readline" errors, and bootstrap.sh expects direnv + .envrc. Also 1Password CLI isn't available in this container. Who's the best person to flag for help?

josh: welcome Harper! Crostini is quirky. Quick notes:
- Docker: Crostini often doesn't have a systemd-managed dockerd. Two options: run Docker on a remote dev host and point DOCKER_HOST to it (or tunnel over SSH), or install podman + podman-docker for better compatibility. Example remote tunnel: `ssh -L 2375:localhost:2375 user@devbox -N` then `export DOCKER_HOST=tcp://localhost:2375`.
- asdf builds: you need the usual dev deps (pkg-config, libreadline, ncurses, etc). Try: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev curl git`

priya: +1 to Josh. For readability, here's the exact set I use in Crostini: `sudo apt install -y build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libncurses-dev xz-utils libffi-dev` then restart your shell and retry `asdf install`.

harper: thanks 44d. I tried installing those packages; node still failed complaining about OpenSSL linkage. Is brew an option inside Crostini?

josh: you can install linuxbrew in Crostini but it's extra friction. If you don't want brew, install `libssl-dev` from apt. If you do use brew then `brew install openssl@1.1` and export LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS before asdf build: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib" && export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"` then `asdf install nodejs 16.20.0`.

harper: got it. About docker: I prefer not to spin up a remote devbox. How good is podman here?

lucas: podman works okay for many compose workflows if you `sudo dnf/apt install podman podman-docker`. On Debian that looks like `sudo apt install -y podman podman-docker`. Note: `podman-compose` parity isn't perfect for some newer Compose V2 features. If tests rely on docker-specific behavior, use the remote host approach or the CI container we provide.

priya: on the .envrc/direnv piece: create a placeholder `.env.local` from `env.example` with fake values, then a minimal `.envrc` like `export $(cat .env.local | xargs)` and run `direnv allow`. That unblocks bootstrap until infra gives you real secrets.

harper: 1Password CLI: there's no official .deb for this environment. Can infra provision a short-lived token or should I copy secrets manually for now?

infra-bot: [onboarding] Created ticket ONB-1201 for Harper to get 1Password CLI access and temporary repo secrets. Infra will follow up with options (token vs manual seed).

harper: awesome, thanks. One more: VS Code Remote / code-server - I usually run code-server inside Crostini but it wants to write to ~/.local and sometimes fails with /etc/ssl cert issues. Any tips for running editors?

josh: if code-server is flaky, try running VS Code on your ChromeOS host and use the "Remote - SSH" extension to connect into Crostini, or run `code` via the official Linux beta if available. For certs, install ca-certificates: `sudo apt install -y ca-certificates`. Also ensure `~/.local/share/code-server` is writable by your user (it should be if you're running as you).

harper: thanks, installing ca-certificates fixed the TLS errors. After the deps and openssl fix, asdf installed python 3.11 and node 18. I copied `server/.tool-versions` to repo root as suggested in the handbook and bootstrap.sh progressed.

lucas: small tip: Crostini sessions may not honor `newgrp` the same way as full distros. If you install docker/podman and add your user to the group, fully close the Linux terminal window and reopen it (or restart the container) so group changes take effect.

harper: useful to know. Final question: what quickchecks do you run before pinging eng for a CI run?

priya: run `make ci-local` (fast suite), `scripts/check-env` (ensures required envs present), and `make lint`. If those pass, open a PR and tag your onboarding buddy.

harper: brilliant, everything passing now. I'll add these Crostini-specific notes to my onboarding doc for other Pixelbook folks. Thanks everyone for the quick help 64f!

josh: welcome aboard, Harper. Ping if you want a pairing session on the local stack.
